holidays.name: Fish Fingers and Custard Day
holidays.description: A day for Doctor Who fans to dunk crispy fish sticks into a bowl of warm custard, as the Eleventh Doctor did. Some fans say it's surprisingly tasty. Others say it's a crime against dinner.
holidays.origin: The day honors the 2010 episode 'The Eleventh Hour'. In it, the freshly regenerated Doctor, played by Matt Smith, tried several foods before settling on fish fingers dipped in custard. Fans turned the scene into an unofficial yearly celebration.
holidays.funFact: The scene was so memorable that fans still cite it as the moment Matt Smith's Doctor became his own man. Many viewers tried the combination at home, and reactions are famously split.

holidays.name: National Find a Rainbow Day
holidays.description: A day to look up, step outside and hunt for a rainbow. If the sky doesn't cooperate, you can spot one in a garden hose mist, a prism, a window sun-catcher or a child's chalk drawing.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It fits April's showers and spring sunshine, the season when rainbows are most likely to appear.
holidays.funFact: Every rainbow is a full circle. From the ground you usually see only the top arc, because the horizon cuts off the rest. From a plane you can sometimes see the whole ring.

holidays.name: National Chocolate Mousse Day
holidays.description: A day to enjoy a silky, airy cloud of chocolate. Whip one up from scratch or grab a spoon and a cup from your favorite bistro.
holidays.origin: Mousse became popular in France in the 1800s, and the dessert has been a favorite of chocolate lovers ever since. This food holiday is an unofficial observance of unclear origin.
holidays.funFact: The word 'mousse' means 'foam' in French. The dessert's lightness comes from air whipped into eggs, cream or both.
